plans.name: 2-day UPPER-LOWER
plans.introAndHelp:
2-day UPPER-LOWER
Welcome to the 2-day Upper-Lower split, here i will explain everything that you will need to know!

First let me tell you, how i structured this training plan.

You will see, that there is 4 different days, even tho this is just a 2-day split. Let me tell you why.

Every day has a number added to it. They either have number 1 or 2. So what you will do, is that one
the first week, you will use the UPPER1 and LOWER1.

And on the second week, you will use UPPER2 and LOWER2. And on the third week, you start again
from UPPER1 and LOWER1, and you continue this cycle over and over!

Now let me show you when to take rest days, and in which order you should run this training plan.

Since this is a 2-day split, you have a lot of freedom, when it comes to the rest days and the order of
the workouts.

You can basically schedule the days however you want. The only requirement being, that you take
atleast 2-3days rest between the training sessions.


Help
Always follow the order that the exercises are written in.

Definitely use different weight for different rep ranges, you always have to adjust. For example, if you
are doing a horizontal push for 5-8reps, you should always choose a heavier weight, than if you did it
for 8-12reps!

Below the name of every bodypart, you can see what type of exercise you are supposed to do, and in
the parentheses are example exercises that you should use, you can pick any of these exercises that i
included there, its up to you what you like, and what you have access to!

If you need any further assistance, or if something is not clear to you, feel free to join my discord, and
i will help you out!


Note
Always write down the weight, sets, and reps of the exercises that you did, so you can keep track of
your progression, this is very important!

3-day UPPER-LOWER

First let me tell you, how i structured this training plan.

This training plan, puts more emphasis on the upper body, because it has 2 upper body sessions and
only 1 lower body session.

Now let me show you when to take rest days, and in which order you should run this training plan.

You should run this program in this order: UPPER1->LOWER1->UPPER2

4-day UPPER-LOWER
Welcome to the 4-day Upper-Lower split, here i will explain everything that you will need to know!

First let me tell you, how i structured this training plan.

This one is very straight forward, 4 different days, and 4 different workouts. Each one is putting more
emphasis on a different bodypart each time.

Now let me show you when to take rest days, and in which order you should run this training plan.

You should run this training plan in this order: UPPER1->LOWER1->UPPER2->LOWER2

You got a couple of options when it comes to the rest days. But i would generally recommend to take
1 or 2 rest days, after you finish the first UPPER1 and LOWER1 workouts. And then the same after
UPPER2 and LOWER2, so it can look something like this:

day1__UPPER1

day2__LOWER1

day3__rest

day4__UPPER2

day5__LOWER2

day6__rest

day7__rest

5-day UPPER-LOWER

one more extra upper body session, to focus more on your arms!

Now let me show you when to take rest days, and in which order you should run this training plan.

You should run this training plan in this order: UPPER1->LOWER1->UPPER2->LOWER2->UPPER3

supplements.title: Cardio
supplements.text:
Cardio
You should do 150minutes of cardio of moderate intensity per week. It doesnt really matter how you
decide to spread this time over the week, but i would NOT recommend doing all the 150minutes at
once, split it into at least 2 sessions minimum.

Dont do cardio before you go train with weights, doing it after your weight training is better, but
definitely not ideal.

I would recommend you to separate your cardio from lifting weights completely. Either do cardio on
an off day, or if you for example lift weights in the morning, then do your cardio in the evening. So
that there is at least 6hours between your cardio and your lifting session.

I recommend low impact exercises, like „fast“ walking. There is no need to do HIIT cardio, as it can be
very hard to recover from. LISS (Low intensity steady state cardio) is king.

Keep in mind, that you shouldnt do excessive amounts of hard to recover from cardio. Like biking for
hours and stuff like that. And if you do, always re-feed after your cardio session, to minimize the
muscle loss as much as possible!

supplements.text:
Which one to pick?
If you dont know which variation you should choose, you should always keep in mind, that you
should pick the one that fits your schedule the most. And also pick according to your experience
level, if you are relatively new to the gym, dont immediately jump to the 6-day variation.

2-day UPPER-LOWER
If you are very busy, but you still want to get the work done, this workout will give you a wide variety
of exercises, that will hit every muscle that you need to, in just 2 days!

3-day UPPER-LOWER
This training plan, is more focused on the upper body, so if thats your priority, and you only got 3
days to go to the gym, then this is the pick for you!

4-day UPPER-LOWER
A well balanced 4-day routine, i recommend it to people who just exited their beginner stage!

5-day UPPER-LOWER
This routine has 3upper body days and 2lower body days, and the extra upper body day, is more
focused on your arms, so if you want to specifically focus on getting bigger arms, then pick this one!

6-day UPPER-LOWER
I recommend this routine to people who already have some experience with lifting, it brings the
maximum amount of volume, so its ideal if you want to take your training to the next level!

supplements.filename: How to add Abs to your routine.pdf
supplements.title: How to add Abs to your routine
supplements.text:
How to add Abs to your routine
I didnt include any ab exercises directly into any routine.

Here, i will show you how to add them to your routine if you want.

You should train your abs atleast 2 timer per week, but you can go up to 4 times per week if you are
able to recover between the sessions.

I recommend you to add 3sets of machine/cable crunch in the 8-15rep range.

And if you dont have access to the machine crunch or to the cables. Start doing weighted sit-ups,
either put a plate or a dumbbel on your chest, and you can easily overload this way!

It doesnt really matter, which day you decide to do the abs on, its purely up to you, you can for
example add them to the days that take you the least time to complete!

So just do 3sets of either machine/cable crunch or weighted sit-ups, in the 8-15rep range, at the end
of the workout of your choice!

supplements.filename: How to add Forearms to your routine.pdf
supplements.title: How to add Forearms to your routine
supplements.text:
How to add Forearms to your routine
There are 3 methods that i recommend.

1.You can add 3sets of wrist curls at the end of each workout, in the 8-12rep range, i like doing this
with the barbell, you roll the bar all the way to your fingertips and back, really trying to feel the
stretch at both ends. But keep in mind, that if you add both abs and wrist curls at the end of every
workout, it might take a little bit longer!

2.If you have access to grippers, you can do them instead of wrist curls, or you can do both wrist curls
and grippers. In the best case scenario, you own a pair of grippers yourself, and you can just do them
at home, whenever you find it convenient, but dont do them before your workout, as it might
negatively impact your workout. Use the same technique and rep range as for the wrist curls.

3.Start doing rice bucket training, not a lot of people know about this technique. This is really going
to blow-up your forearms and hand muscles. All you need is a bucket and like 10lbs of rice. Then you
can do it at the comfort of your home! If you want to try it out, i recommend this follow-along
routine: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iVum3vWlh4Q

You might get very sore when trying it out for the first time, so always wait until you are not sore
anymore, and then you can go again! Eventually you might be able to do this everyday.

supplements.title: How to warm up
supplements.text:
How to warm up
Always warm-up properly before you start working out. Do some stretches for the most important
joints, like shoulders, wrists, elbows, knees, hips and ankles. It doesnt need to be anything fancy, just
some basic stretches that you used to do in school. You will know that you are ready, when your
joints dont feel stiff and cold anymore. You can also do like 5-10minutes on the treadmill or elliptical,
to get your blood going so you feel ready for action!

After that, you should always slowly build up on the first exercise that you are doing.

Lets say you are doing bench press as your first exercise of the day.

Start with doing couple of reps with an empty bar, then put on roughly 50% of your working weight
on the bar – and do like 3-4reps with it. Then put on 75% of your working weight on the bar, and do
2-3reps with it. Then you are ready to start your actual working sets!
